chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever dies and has no heir from his close relatives (qarabah) nor a mawla of 'itaqah (manumission) who has guaranteed his debt, then his wealth is from the anfal (public treasury/fay').

key_terms.مَوْلَى عَتَاقَةٍ: mawla of manumission (client freed by a master)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the wealth of a Shia Muslim who dies with no close relatives or mawla heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the final stage of inheritance distribution, where the absence of both agnatic relatives (asabah) and mawla al-itaqah results in the estate becoming 'anfal' (public treasury). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the Imam or Caliph acts as the ultimate heir when no specific kin or manumission client exists, ensuring the wealth serves the broader Muslim community. It highlights the systematic hierarchy of heirs, moving from close kin to the public treasury, reflecting the comprehensive nature of Shia inheritance law.
